evidence: Source reads/edits and manual reference review only; no tests, builds, syntax checks, UI automation, encoder/export, project/helper/game execution, process inspection or Bedrock launch

sourcePort.range: ExportRange retains integer fromMs/toMs. Its constructor applies Java's one-millisecond minimum; decoding/validation rejects unordered, out-of-day or over-two-hour selections
sourcePort.count: Estimate the last index with integer arithmetic, then apply Java's actual double division/multiplication/addition endpoint predicate. This preserves the endpoint decision instead of assuming duration*FPS always lands on the same rounded double
sourcePort.ui: Select export range exposes start/end times and derives frame count at the chosen FPS; Use camera path range takes its earliest/latest key times. A range uses the existing world-rebuild path and cannot silently become a playhead export
sourcePort.worker: The selected range, start and derived frame count pass through ReplayVideoRequest into ExportOptions. Validation rejects disagreement before native export operations
sourcePort.sourceBounds: Before world reset, a selected start cannot be clamped to a later bootstrap time and its end cannot exceed recording duration. After reset, the actual attached replay origin must still equal the requested start
sourcePort.camera: Existing camera sampling uses absolute replay timestamps from the validated origin; keyframes are not shifted or rebased to clip zero
sourcePort.endpointBudget: Indexed capture, native timeline, built-in stream encoder and decoded audit/comparison allow at most FPS*7200+1 samples, permitting the sample at exactly two hours. Real-time capture retains its prior FPS*7200 budget
sourcePort.intent: New exports use intent schema 4 and arctic-bedrock-export-intent-v4 hash domain. Optional selectedRange is content-bound and validated against origin/FPS/frame count; frame-count mode leaves it absent
sourcePort.legacy: Intent schemas 1..3 keep their original hash domains, omitted-field serialization and old sample limits. Schema 4 keeps the same explicit encoding-profile and native cadence checks
sourcePort.comparison: Paired export diagnostics identify selectedRange differences even if two end selections happen to produce the same set of sample timestamps
sourcePort.unchangedProof: Range selection is not native simulation, shader/appearance, GPU presentation, audio or deterministic video evidence
